**Step:** [step-10](../README.md) — From iteration 4's evidence alone, which approved drugs do its independent generators (the PrimeKG walk, the phenotype twin, a screen-wide PRISM sweep, LINCS signature reversal) converge on beyond chance, and which of those survive every iteration-4 check (mechanism direction, the child's own safety, a decoy)?
**Status:** refuted  |  **Confidence:** 0.15  |  **Revisions:** 2
**Gene:** —  |  **Path:** s10-convergence

## The claim

P4-29: iteration 4's independent drug generators converge on the same approved drugs more often than chance

**Prediction if true.** Four generator lists, each fixed by a rule before the join: (1) the PrimeKG walk's top 50 openFDA-labelled drugs (entry 142); (2) the phenotype twin's approved analogues (entry 150, model_interventions.tsv); (3) PRISM: the union of the top 0.5 % of eligible Launched compounds on each contrast of the screen-wide sweep; (4) LINCS: approved drugs in both engines' top 100 reversers (E3). Drugs are joined on one normalised name. The count of approved drugs named by 2 or more generators exceeds the 95th percentile of a 10,000-draw null that replaces each list with an equal-sized random draw from that generator's own approved universe (one-sided p < 0.05). Retrospective note, stated before the join: entry 151 already placed dasatinib at the 99.4th percentile of all compounds on the aneuploidy contrast and entry 150 already names it as the twin's approved analogue, so the report gives the count with and without dasatinib

**What would refute it.** No drug is named by 2 or more generators, or the observed count is at or below the null's 95th percentile
